slides.say: b and y are integers. Given: y is equal to b minus three, squared, plus b plus eight, cubed. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
So all the choices are about even and odd. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, dropping the powers, and then plugging in numbers.

[short pause] Let's start by dropping the powers. Remember, a power doesn't change parity. So in a parity question I may drop it, and I'd never do that in a regular equation. b minus three plus b plus eight is two b plus five.
at: never do that in a regular equation
b minus three plus b plus eight

slides.say: Two b is always even, whatever b is, and even plus five is odd. So y is always odd. Choice number four is our answer.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: And here's why, without letters. b plus eight and b minus three are eleven apart, an odd gap, so one is even and the other is odd. Odd plus even is odd.

[pause] Now let's try plugging in. It's easier to choose b than y. b is one. One minus three is negative two, and squared is four. One plus eight is nine, and nine cubed is seven twenty-nine. Four plus seven twenty-nine is seven thirty-three, odd.
b is two. Two minus three is negative one, and squared is one. Two plus eight is ten, and ten cubed is a thousand. One plus a thousand is a thousand one, odd again.
So b can be odd or even, and choice numbers one and three are out. y was odd both times, so choice number two is out. Choice number four. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: b can be odd or even
